_note: Hand-authored before the scorer existed. See README.md in this directory. `base` names a document from `documents`; `response` is the raw model output as it would arrive.

cases.response:

cases.reason: The intended element's fill is the requested colour. Every other element is byte-identical. Nothing else changed, so this is the ideal response.

cases.name: recolor_wrong_element
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#ff0000"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: A confident, well-formed, correctly-executed edit to the wrong element. This is the central failure mode the instrument exists to measure.

cases.name: recolor_target_and_one_other
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#ff0000"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#ff0000"/>
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: Hedging. The target did receive the requested edit, so identification succeeded, but an unrequested element changed too. Strict must fail; loose must pass. This is the behaviour that motivated the whole project, so it needs its own class rather than being folded into correct or wrong.

cases.name: recolor_all_candidates
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#ff0000"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#ff0000"/>
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#ff0000"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: The degenerate hedge: edit everything and be guaranteed to include the target. Loose accuracy alone would score this as success, which is why loose is never reported without the collateral count beside it.

cases.name: reordered_attributes_only
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path fill="#3b6ea5" id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}"/>
  <path fill="#ff0000" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" id="e22222222"/>
  <path d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310" id="e33333333"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: Attribute order carries no meaning in XML. Two of the three elements have reordered attributes and are otherwise untouched; counting them as collateral would measure serialisation habits.

cases.name: non_rendering_attribute_added
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#3b6ea5" data-note="unchanged"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#ff0000"/>
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: A `data-note` attribute changes nothing a viewer sees. Collateral is defined over rendering-relevant attributes, because the instruction is about the picture.

cases.name: reordered_elements
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#ff0000"/>
  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: Alignment is by identity, not by position. Reordering changes z-order in principle, but these shapes do not overlap and no rendering-relevant attribute differs. A position-based aligner would report three wrong elements here, which is why this fixture exists.

cases.name: renamed_ids_tokens_preserved
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="shape1" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="shape2" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#ff0000"/>
  <path id="shape3" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: The model renamed every id but preserved the geometry tokens. The token is unique per element and preserved by contract, so it is the primary identity anchor and survives exactly this. Recorded as tier TOKEN so reliance on the weaker tiers stays visible.

cases.name: stroke_added_to_target
cases.response:

  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>

cases.name: right_element_wrong_operation
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#000000"/>
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: The model found the right element and performed the wrong edit - it recoloured instead of outlining. Identification succeeded, execution failed. This is precisely why the two are reported separately: a single correct/incorrect bit would blame reference resolution for an execution error. The outcome class is not CORRECT_* because the requested edit did not happen.

cases.name: delete_target
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: For `delete`, absence IS the correct edit. The aligner must distinguish absent-and-expected from absent-and-not, or every successful deletion would score as a malformed response.

cases.name: rotate_target_exact
cases.response:

  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#3b6ea5" transform="rotate(90)"/>

cases.name: rotate_target_congruent
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#3b6ea5" transform="rotate(450)"/>
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: 450 degrees renders identically to 90. This instrument exists to distinguish the rendered layer from the source layer, so rejecting a rendering-identical edit for a cosmetic reason would contradict its own premise. Rotation is compared modulo 360.

cases.name: rotate_target_wrong_angle
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#3b6ea5" transform="rotate(45)"/>
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: Right element, wrong angle. 45 is not congruent to 90 modulo 360, so this is an execution failure rather than a notation difference.

cases.name: unchanged_document
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: The document came back semantically identical with no explanation. Distinct from abstention: the model made no claim about being unable to answer, it simply did nothing.

cases.name: abstention_explicit
cases.response: I cannot determine which shape is the top-left one, because the path data is redacted and the markup contains no positional information. Please provide the rendered image or coordinates.
cases.reason: The epistemically correct response to a provably under-determined instruction. Scoring it as failure would make the metric reward confident guessing, while the project's own motivation is that models hedge under ambiguity.

cases.name: abstention_with_unchanged_document
cases.response:
The markup does not say which element is top-left, so I am returning it unchanged rather than guessing:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: An explicit refusal accompanied by an unedited document. The refusal is the operative signal; a valid SVG alongside it must not downgrade this to NO_EDIT, or a model that explains itself would score worse than one that stays silent.

cases.name: abstention_phrased_as_question
cases.response: Which of the three shapes did you mean? I have no way to tell them apart from this markup - they share a tag and a fill, and the geometry is redacted.
cases.reason: A clarifying question is a refusal to guess. Third phrasing, included because the abstention detector is a classifier and a single phrasing would leave it fitted to one wording.

cases.name: whitespace_only
cases.reason: Empty output is not an abstention. Abstention requires an explicit claim that the information is insufficient; silence makes no claim at all, and crediting it would flatter a model that simply failed.

cases.name: unparseable_xml
cases.response: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path id="e11111111" fill="#3b6ea5"</svg>
cases.reason: Broken markup. Scored, never discarded - the denominator is fixed at freeze time, so a malformed response must consume a case rather than vanish from it.

cases.name: svg_inside_code_fence
cases.response:
Here is the edited SVG:

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#ff0000"/>
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
</svg>
```

I changed the second path's fill to red.
cases.reason: Prose and code fences around a correct edit. Extraction must find the SVG, or format compliance would be scored as identification failure - which is the exact misattribution ADR-0006 exists to prevent.

cases.name: numeric_formatting_difference
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e11111111" d="{{GEOM_aaaaaaaa}}" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#3b6ea5" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="3.0"/>
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: 3.0 and 3 are the same width. Numeric comparison uses the configured tolerance.

cases.name: geometry_token_altered
cases.response:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <path id="e11111111" d="M 0 0 L 10 0 L 10 10 Z" fill="#3b6ea5"/>
  <path id="e22222222" d="{{GEOM_bbbbbbbb}}" fill="#ff0000"/>
  <path id="e33333333" d="{{GEOM_cccccccc}}" fill="#d9b310"/>
</svg>
cases.reason: The model invented geometry for an element it was told to leave alone. The target edit is correct, so identification succeeded, but `d` is rendering-relevant and its change is collateral. Alignment falls back to id because the token no longer matches - recorded so reliance on the weaker tier is visible.
